uncited: This article builds on [Rigid Body Transformation (SE3)](11475-rigid-body-transformation-se3.md).
The family operates on the Special Euclidean group SE(3), which consists of all rigid transformations in 3D space.
A rigid transformation $T$ is defined by a rotation matrix $R \in SO(3)$ and a translation vector $t \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
To perform these operations linearly, points and vectors are represented in homogeneous coordinates.
A 3D point $p = (x, y, z)$ is represented as $p_h = (x, y, z, 1)^T$, while a direction vector $v = (x, y, z)$ is represented as $v_h = (x, y, z, 0)^T$.
The distinction is critical: appending 1 allows translation to affect the position, while appending 0 ensures translation does not affect the direction.
where $R$ is a $3 \times 3$ orthogonal matrix with determinant 1, and $t$ is a $3 \times 1$ column vector.
The bottom row is $[0, 0, 0, 1]$ to preserve the homogeneous coordinate.
